ai.title: Fix login modal clipboard errors and enable text selection
ai.summary: Login modal replaces TerminalLink with selectable text and removes direct browser open to fix clipboard errors. `useClipboard` tracks selection state for visual feedback, while `copyTextToClipboard` discards stderr via `stdio` options to prevent TUI corruption on headless servers. Keyboard handlers now fire-and-forget async copy operations. Changes affect CLI components and hooks, specifically `login-modal.tsx`, `use-clipboard.ts`, and `clipboard.ts`.

eli5.text: When you log in through the command line, the login screen no longer tries to open your web browser automatically (which was causing errors) and instead shows the login link as selectable text you can highlight and copy yourself. The tool now also handles copying that link to your clipboard more quietly in the background, suppressing error messages that could mess up the text-based interface on headless servers. If you look, you'll notice you can select and copy the login URL directly from the screen, and the visual feedback confirms your selection is ready to paste.

ai.title: Gravity ads cache and cycle when fetches stop
ai.summary: cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts caches fetched ads and cycles them when new fetches stop, replacing the hard rotation pause after 3 ads without activity. The hook tracks idle state via isUserActive with a 30s threshold, pausing new fetches while continuing to serve cached ads. Controller state is consolidated into a single ref, replacing multiple refs and useCallback chains.

eli5.text: When you stop interacting with the assistant, ads now stay visible and cycle through previously fetched ones instead of stopping after three ads. The system keeps a small cache of up to 50 ads and continues rotating them while new fetching is paused during 30 seconds of inactivity. You would see the same ad reappear less often, and new ads resume fetching when you start typing again.

ai.title: CLI version bumped to 1.0.596
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI package version incremented from 1.0.595 to 1.0.596 in cli/release/package.json. This release-bump commit carries the cumulative user-visible changes shipped since 1.0.595, including the renamed and expanded gpt-5-agent (formerly thinker-gpt-5) with file edit tools and high-effort reasoning, the new opus-agent alongside it in the general agent factory, and the associated agent:gpt-5 and agent:opus slash commands in the CLI picker. Additional release contents cover a more aggressive advisory lock health check (10s interval, pg_locks ownership verification), TSX editor formatter defaulting to vscode.typescript-language-features, a tweaked /new command description, a hardened login modal clipboard flow, gravity ad caching on fetch stalls, and a web UI hero tagline update.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version field incremented from 1.0.595 to 1.0.596 (diff line 3, +/-1 lines).

eli5.text: This release adds new AI agent options and improves reliability for database connections, plus a faster, higher-quality coding experience on the web. The GPT-5 thinking agent now spawns file-finder helpers in parallel and was joined by a brand-new Opus agent, both reachable through fresh slash commands like '/agent:opus'. The landing page hero now boasts '100+ seconds faster than Claude Code,' and the login modal stops clipboard crashes while letting you highlight and copy text. Background ad serving now caches and recycles ads when idle, so you keep seeing relevant offers without the feed freezing. On the technical side, the database lock health checker now catches lost locks ten seconds sooner to prevent stuck sessions, and the TypeScript formatter switched to the built-in editor tool to fix inconsistent TSX formatting. Upgrading gives you a snappier, more stable AI coding companion that surfaces the right files and agents automatically, with clearer web messaging and fewer hiccups during login or heavy usage.

ai.title: Add env var substitution for MCP config
ai.summary: Adds substituteEnvInValue and substituteEnvInRecord helpers in common/src/mcp/client.ts to expand $VAR_NAME references within MCP configuration values. These helpers process stdio transport envs, and http/sse transport headers, interpolating strings like 'Bearer $TOKEN'. If a referenced environment variable is undefined, the original literal string is preserved.

eli5.text: When you connect the assistant to an external tool, that tool often needs a secret password sent along with the request. You can now write that password in your settings as a placeholder like $TOKEN, and the system replaces it with the real secret value automatically before sending it out. If you forget to set the secret, you get the placeholder text back exactly as written, so nothing breaks silently. This is live today for anyone using these external tool connections.

The release ships a renamed and expanded gpt-5-agent (formerly thinker-gpt-5) with file edit tools and high-effort reasoning alongside a new opus-agent in the general agent factory, exposed via the agent:gpt-5 and agent:opus slash commands, plus a hardened login modal clipboard flow, gravity ad caching on fetch stalls, the web UI hero tagline update, and a more aggressive advisory lock health check. eli5.text: This release lets you securely plug external tools into Freebuff using dynamic configuration that automatically fills in your secret tokens and credentials, so MCP-powered tools work correctly in your terminal without exposing sensitive values in plain text. If a referenced secret is missing, the system gracefully falls back to the original configuration text instead of breaking, keeping your setup stable. Upgrading gives you safer, cleaner integration with third-party tools and services, so you can connect MCP-compatible utilities to Freebuff without worrying about leaking credentials or managing sensitive values by hand.
